scope: Prevent a stale drop event from reordering dock regions after Escape canceled the active desktop drag.

source_control.push: Normal fast-forward push; remote ref verified at the exact runtime commit.

finding.reproduction: After Escape cleared the active drag state, the drop handler still trusted a stale text/plain payload and could apply the canceled dock reorder if a late drop event arrived.
finding.fix: The drop handler now requires a current drag source and verifies that it matches the source id in the event payload. A stale, canceled, or mismatched drop is ignored and clears any transient preview without persisting an order or announcing success.
finding.regression_test: Real Chromium starts a drag, previews the target, dispatches Escape, then dispatches a late drop with the old DataTransfer. It verifies the original order and stored value are unchanged, the preview/dragging state is cleared, no completion announcement is emitted, and the normal subsequent drag still works.
finding.initial_test_attempt: The first targeted test attempt failed because the test asserted a nested result property while the browser callback returned a flat object. The assertion was corrected; the focused test and full suite then passed.
preserved_contracts: valid desktop drag-and-drop continues to reorder the three existing workspace regions
canceled or stale drag cannot alter local dock order
dock configuration remains outside the Page Model
Save and Publish remain separate and are not invoked by docking
canvas size and non-overlap rules remain unchanged

implementation.reuse_review: Reused the existing native desktop dock drag/drop state and its Escape cleanup; no outside runtime code or new dependency was needed for this defensive lifecycle check.
